title: A smooth filtered colimit with Noetherian fibres is regular
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $J$ a small nonempty filtered category, and $(A_j)_{j\in J}$ a diagram of commutative $R$-algebras with $R$-algebra transition maps [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Suppose each $R\to A_j$ is smooth [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and let $B=\varinjlim_j A_j$ be its colimit in commutative $R$-algebras. If for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ the fibre ring $B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], then $R\to B$ is regular [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]: it is flat and its fibre rings are geometrically regular. Tensor products use [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with $(b\otimes c)(b'\otimes c')=bb'\otimes cc'$ and unit $1\otimes1$.

source.place: Tag 07EP, lemma-colimit-smooth-regular, statement and proof at lines 10458–10483; small filtered-diagram formulation of the directed-system statement.

proof.text: Each $A_j$ is flat over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat]. The algebra colimit cocone with apex $B$ is also a colimit of the underlying $R$-modules by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-underlying-module], since $J$ is small and filtered. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-flat-modules] makes $B$ a flat $R$-module. No Noetherian assumption on $R$ or $B$ is used.

source.place: Tag 07EP, lemma-colimit-smooth-regular, proof, first sentence (Algebra 00TA and 05UT).

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $F=B\otimes_R k$; $F$ is Noetherian by hypothesis. Let $K/k$ be any finite purely inseparable extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Put $C=K\otimes_R B$ and $C_j=K\otimes_R A_j$, with $K$ an $R$-algebra via $R\to k\to K$. Tensor cancellation [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] with $S=k$, $A=K$ gives $K\otimes_k(k\otimes_R B)\cong C$. Symmetry $k\otimes_R B\cong F$, given by $a\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes a$ and its inverse, therefore identifies $K\otimes_k F$ with $C$. Choose a finite $k$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ of $K$. The elements $e_i\otimes1$ generate $K\otimes_k F$ over $F$: write each first tensor factor in that basis and use bilinearity [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] makes $K\otimes_k F$, and hence $C$, Noetherian. This supplies the Noetherian hypothesis implicit in the Stacks proof.

source.place: Tag 07EP, lemma-colimit-smooth-regular, proof, finite purely inseparable extension and displayed tensor identity; implicit Noetherianity uses Algebra 00FN.

proof.text: We check that $C$ is the colimit of the rings $C_j$. Work in a common universe containing $J$, its morphisms, and all rings under consideration, so the universe hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-tensor-elementwise] holds. Apply that node with $N=K$ and use tensor symmetry: $C$ is the colimit of the $R$-modules $C_j$, every element comes from one stage, and the coprojections $\gamma_j:C_j\to C$ are ring maps. Given a compatible ring cocone $f_j:C_j\to T$, equip $T$ with its $R$-algebra structure using any one $f_j$. This is independent of $j$: maps from two indices to a common index identify their composites with $R$. The $f_j$ are now $R$-linear, so the module colimit gives a unique $R$-linear $f:C\to T$ with $f\gamma_j=f_j$. For $x,y\in C$, represent both at a common stage $j$ using filteredness and the representation assertion. Then $f(xy)=f_j(x_jy_j)=f_j(x_j)f_j(y_j)=f(x)f(y)$; also $f(1)=f_j(1)=1$. Hence $f$ is a ring map. Conversely any ring map with these factorizations is $R$-linear and is the same $f$. This proves the ring-colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] without assuming that arbitrary algebra colimits preserve underlying modules.

source.place: Tag 07EP, lemma-colimit-smooth-regular, proof, displayed equality with the colimit (Algebra 00DD and 00D6), ring universal property written out.

proof.text: The map $K\to C_j=K\otimes_R A_j$ is smooth by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition]. Since $K$ is a field, [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local] says that every localization of $C_j$ at a prime is regular local. Fix a prime $\mathfrak q\subset C$ and let $\mathfrak q_j=\gamma_j^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-localization-at-prime], the rings $L_j=(C_j)_{\mathfrak q_j}$ form a filtered diagram with colimit $L=C_{\mathfrak q}$. Its transition maps are local: for an arrow $a:j\to j'$ and a fraction $x/s\in L_j$, its image belongs to the maximal ideal of $L_{j'}$ exactly when $C(a)(x)\in\mathfrak q_{j'}$, equivalently $x\in\mathfrak q_j$, exactly when $x/s$ belongs to the maximal ideal of $L_j$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Here the denominator stays outside the prime by contraction. Each $L_j$ is regular local, and $L$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], applied to the Noetherian ring $C$ from step 2.

source.place: Tag 07EP, lemma-colimit-smooth-regular, proof, smooth base change (00T4), regularity at the stages (00TT), localization of the filtered colimit (037D), Noetherian localization (00FN).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal] to $J$ and the localized diagram of step 4. It supplies a small nonempty directed system of the same regular local rings with the same colimit $L$; all its transition maps are still local, since they are maps from the original localized diagram. The hypotheses of [lem-per-noetherian-local-colimit-regular] are therefore satisfied: regular local stages, local transition maps, and Noetherian apex $L$. Consequently $C_{\mathfrak q}=L$ is regular local. Since $\mathfrak q$ was arbitrary and $C$ is Noetherian, $C$ is a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Tag 07EP, lemma-colimit-smooth-regular, proof, last sentence: Algebra 07DX; passage from small filtered categories to directed sets is Categories 0032.

proof.text: For the chosen prime $\mathfrak p$, the fibre $F$ is Noetherian and step 5 proves that $K\otimes_k F\cong C$ is regular for every finite purely inseparable extension $K/k$. Hence $F$ is geometrically regular over $k$ by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. This applies to every $\mathfrak p\subset R$. Together with flatness from step 1, it is precisely the definition in that node of a regular ring map $R\to B$. The zero fibre causes no exception: it is Noetherian and has no prime localizations to check.

source.place: Tag 07EP, lemma-colimit-smooth-regular, proof, conclusion, using the definitions recalled in Section 07BY (Definition 07BZ and Algebra 0382).
